key_insight: Collaborating AI agents derived and experimentally tested a minimum-calibration result for quantum spins in diamond, rejecting an initially promising but drift-affected experiment as inconclusive.
engineering_relevance: Agent-based cross-checks and reference measurements offer a route to more reliable autonomous characterization of quantum hardware.
method: Generate and critique research questions, with authority to stop or redirect investigations.
Derive minimum calibration requirements for a defined family of microwave pulse sequences and check them computationally.
Design discriminating experiments and revise measurement protocols when reference measurements reveal drift.
evidence_signal: The initial experiment was deemed inconclusive because of signal drift; a revised experiment met unchanged acceptance criteria and supported the theoretical predictions.
watch_item: The demonstration concerns a defined pulse-sequence family and diamond spin ensembles; broader hardware applicability and quantitative performance are not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Collaborative AI agents for autonomous experimental research with solid-state quantum spins
